subject: general
question: What is the IUPAC rule for writing element symbols?

options.text: First letter uppercase, second lowercase (in case of two letters)
Both letters always in uppercase form (in case of two letters)
Two lowercase letters always used (in case of two letters)

solution:
The correct answer is __**First letter uppercase, second lowercase (in case of two letters)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry** (**IUPAC**) is the global authority that approves the names of elements and their symbols.
 
• According to **IUPAC** nomenclature rules, the symbol of an element is either **one** or **two letters** of its name in **English** or **Latin**.
 
• The **first letter** of a symbol is always written as a **capital letter** (**uppercase**) and the **second letter** is always written as a **small letter** (**lowercase**). ***Hence, the rule stated in option 1 is correct.***
 
• For example, the symbol for **Hydrogen** is **H** (single letter, uppercase).
